samples.summary: `sanitizeDocStyles` only bands keys in `STYLE_IDS` and passes unknown keys through untouched, but `blockStyleId` can synthesise a non-`STYLE_IDS` key from an unbanded `headingLevel` — so a peer-written registry entry reaches `resolveStyleInline`/`resolveStyleBlock` unbanded, bypassing `normalizeFontSize`/`normalizeLineHeight` document-wide.
samples.evidence: Two peer-writable inputs compose. (1) `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:274` (and the duplicate parser `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:522`) read `block.headingLevel = Number(attrs.headingLevel)` with no band — a Tree attribute of `"2.5"` yields `2.5`, of `"x"` yields `NaN`. (2) `blockStyleId` (named-styles.ts:323) does `Math.min(6, Math.max(1, headingLevel ?? 1))` and interpolates: `2.5` → `'heading-2.5'`, `NaN` → `'heading-NaN'` — neither is in `STYLE_IDS` (named-styles.ts:69-79), so the `for (const id of STYLE_IDS)` loop at line 196 never touches such an entry, and the `{ ...source }` at line 194 copies it through verbatim (asserted by the new test 'leaves a key no reader could resolve alone'). (3) `resolveStyleInline` (line 391) and `resolveStyleBlock` (line 403) then spread `docStyles?.[id]?.inline` / `.block` for that exact synthesised id into every run's base style and into `effectiveBlockSpacing`. Attack: a collaborator calls `doc.update` writing `root.stylesJson = '{"heading-2.5":{"inline":{"fontSize":1e9},"block":{"lineHeight":1e9}}}'` plus one heading block with `headingLevel="2.5"`; `layout.ts:874-878` computes `lineHeight = max(1, 1e9) * fontSize`, i.e. the unbanded geometry this sanitizer was added to prevent, for every reader of the document. The function's own JSDoc asserts the opposite ('an unrecognised key is unreachable anyway (`resolveStyleInline` looks entries up by `StyleId`)'), which is what makes the hole read as covered.

samples.summary: `bandElementNumerics` silently stops banding at `MAX_GROUP_DEPTH` (32) while every consumer of those elements (`flattenElements`, the PDF exporter) recurses with no depth limit — a text body nested 33+ groups deep is rendered but never banded.
samples.evidence: `if (el.type === 'group' && depth < MAX_GROUP_DEPTH)` — at depth 32 the branch is skipped and the function returns the element with its children untouched, rather than rejecting or truncating them. The readers that consume the same tree have no cap: `packages/slides/src/model/group.ts:377 flattenElements` recurses `el.data.children` unbounded, as does `packages/slides/src/export/pdf.ts:222`. The paths where this function is the *only* band are the ones added in this change: `bandSlidesDocumentNumerics` (used by `parseSlidesSnapshot`/`parseBoardSnapshot` in `packages/frontend/src/components/history/snapshot-adapters.ts:53,75`, whose output goes to `MemSlidesStore`, which bands nothing) and `bandLayoutNumerics` for `root.layouts` (`packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:456`), whose `staticElements`/`placeholders` are rendered verbatim (`packages/slides/src/view/canvas/layout-preview.ts:46-63`). Attack: a collaborator's modified client writes a 33-deep group chain with `lineHeight: 1e9`/`fontSize: 1e9` in the innermost text body (the backend PUT cannot do this — `assertValidElementData` throws past `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH`, controller line 769 — but `doc.update` has no such gate); anyone opening that revision or that layout gets the unbanded value. samples.summary: `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` bounds fragments per *row* only, and the individual band ceilings multiply: in-band `fontSize`×`lineHeight` yields a ~700,000 px line, so a few-KB peer-written table still drives 200 pages per row with no document-wide budget.
samples.evidence: `layout.ts:874-878` computes `lineHeight = Math.max(1, resolved.lineHeight) * maxFontSize`. Both factors are *inside* the new bands: `MAX_FONT_SIZE = 4000` pt (≈5333 px after `ptToPx`) and `MAX_LINE_HEIGHT = 132` (`model/numeric-attrs.ts:77,83`), so one legal run yields a ≈704,000 px line — ~815 letter pages — which `computeTableLayout` sums into the row height. The loop at pagination.ts:153 then emits one page and one `PageLine` per iteration up to the per-row cap of 200 (line 178). Nothing caps the number of such rows: a table with 100 single-run cells (≈8 KB of JSON a collaborator can write via `doc.update`, or PUT — the backend band clamps to the same ceilings rather than rejecting) produces ~20,000 pages/`PageLine`s on every reader's main thread. I confirmed the arithmetic and the per-row scope of the bound in code but did not measure the resulting hang, hence low confidence on exploitability rather than on the arithmetic.

finding.summary: The new read-side band is bypassable via the board store, the sibling CRDT path that holds the same verbatim docs blocks
finding.evidence: The change's own rationale (yorkie-slides-store.ts:489-497, docs/design/docs/docs.md) is that a slide text body "passes through no Tree attribute codec", so the guarantee has to live on the read of the CRDT because "nothing stops a collaborator calling doc.update with fontSize: 1e9". Boards store the identical shape and are read by an identical, unbanded parser: `yorkie-board-store.ts:374` (`const blocks = yorkieToPlain<Block[]>(rawData.blocks) ?? []`), `:1319` (withTextElement) and `:1351` (shape text) have no `bandBlockNumerics` call. Board elements are rendered through the slides renderer (`packages/board/src/view/viewport.ts` imports @wafflebase/slides; `packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:239,299` call docs `computeLayout`), so a peer's `doc.update` on a board can store a `type:'table'` block with `columnWidths` of N entries — `computeTableLayout` (packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:153,170-201) allocates a LayoutTableCell per (row, column) pair from `columnWidths.length`, which the board path never caps at MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS — or an `Infinity` rowSpan/padding, for every other viewer of that board. The backend v1 PUT *does* band boards (assertValidBoardBody → assertValidElement → assertValidElementData → assertValidTextBodyBlocks → assertValidSlideBlocks → bandSlideBlockNumerics), so the collaborative path is precisely the writer the PUT band cannot cover.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the board CRDT read path has no numeric band, leaving peer-written Infinity/huge values (e.g. table columnWidths, rowSpan, padding) to reach computeLayout. The file refutes this directly: yorkie-board-store.ts imports bandBlockNumerics (:39) and bandElementNumerics (:26) and applies them on every read and text-mutation path — readElement's text branch bands blocks at :383-385 (the very line the finding quotes as unbanded), the generic tail wraps every other element (shapes/sticky notes with data.text.blocks) in bandElementNumerics at :442-448, group children recurse back through readElement at :425-431, withTextElement bands at :1333-1335, and withShapeText bands at :1368. bandElementNumerics itself descends into data.blocks, data.text.blocks and nested table-cell blocks (packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:46-77), and bandBlockNumerics caps table geometry (packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:293-373). The finding's cited line numbers (374, 1319, 1351) do not correspond to the band call sites in the working tree; the band calls are a few lines below each. The doc comment at :357-368 states the board is banded "exactly as the slides twin does" for precisely the rendering reason the finding gives.
